source.title: Lurgan Mail, 29 April 1933, p. 3 ("Lurgan Rural Council")
source.publisher: Lurgan Mail (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: names from the OCR text, which is clean; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the rural district council (ten electoral divisions), 1933: there was no election. The report prints no party labels. Returned unopposed. J. O'Neill: no party label printed in 1933, and no report of this election states one. The label Nationalist shown before 7 Nov 2026 came from a later statement, not a report of this election: Armagh Guardian, 13 Nov 1931, p. 2 and Frontier Sentinel, 14 Nov 1931, p. 6 (Lurgan Rural Council co-option vote): Mr. Joseph O'Neill (Catholic and Nationalist) proposed for co-option to his late brother James' seat (statement of Nov 1931, before his first election).
